title: Pay yourself first
blurb: Meena never saves what is left, because nothing is left. Learn the small habit that fixes it.
t1.title: The empty purse
t1.hook: Meena earns {income} a month at a kirana shop. Every month she plans to save what is left. Every month, nothing is left.
t1.define: **Paying yourself first** means you set aside your savings on pay day, before you spend on anything else. Saving is a bill you pay to your future self.
t1.analogy: A tea stall owner puts the milk money aside first. Only then does she spend on treats. Savings work the same way.
q1.prompt: Meena starts moving {save} to savings on every pay day. How much will she have set aside after one year? Type a number in rupees.
q2.prompt: Meena wants to save. Which plan is most likely to work?
q2.hint: Which plan makes saving happen before the spending does?
q2.explain: Setting money aside first makes saving certain. What is left over is a hope, not a plan.
q2.opt.a: Save whatever money is left at the end of the month
q2.fb.a: Saving what is left feels fair, but spending quietly grows to use all the money, so very little is ever left.
q2.opt.b: Move {save} to savings on pay day, then spend the rest
q2.opt.c: Wait until she earns more, then begin
q2.opt.d: Save only when she feels like it
t2.title: Small amounts, every month
t2.define: A small amount saved **regularly** beats a big amount saved now and then. What matters most is that you never skip a month.
t2.steps.1: Pick an amount you will hardly miss, like {save} from {income}.
t2.steps.2: Move it on pay day, the same day every month.
t2.steps.3: Treat it like a bill. It is not optional.
q3.prompt: What share of Meena's pay is {save}? Type a percentage.
q3.hint: Divide {save} by {income}, then write it as a percentage.
q3.explain: {save} divided by {income} is {pct}. A small share of her pay.
q4.prompt: Ravi saves {step} every single month. Asha saves a big sum twice, then stops. Who is building a habit?
q4.hint: A habit is something you do again and again.
q4.explain: Ravi shows up every month. Regular saving is what turns into a habit.
q4.opt.b: Asha, because her sum was bigger
t3.title: How long will it take?
t3.steps.1: Asha wants {goal2} for a festival outfit. She saves {ex} a month.
t3.steps.2: Divide the goal by the monthly amount. That gives the months.
t3.steps.3: If it does not divide evenly, round up to a whole month.
t3.note: A smaller amount still gets you there. It only takes more months. Starting now beats waiting for a bigger amount.
q5.prompt: Ravi wants {goal} for a new bag for college. He puts aside {step} each month. How many months will it take?
q5.hint: Divide the goal by the monthly amount.
q6.prompt: Ravi can only spare a small sum each month. What should he do?
q6.hint: Which choice gets money saved this month?
q6.explain: Starting small builds the habit. The sum can grow later.
q6.opt.a: Wait until he can save a big amount
q6.fb.a: It feels better to start big, but waiting means nothing gets saved. Small and regular beats big and never.
q6.opt.b: Start now with a small sum and raise it when his pay rises
q6.opt.d: Give up, it is too little to matter
t4.title: Lab: pay first or spend first
t4.explore: Open the lab. Move the sliders to compare paying yourself first with saving only what is left. Then answer below.
t4.lab.save: Set aside on pay day each month
t4.lab.left: Left over at month end (if you spend first)
t4.lab.payFirst: Saved in a year, paying first
t4.lab.spendFirst: Saved in a year, spending first
q7.prompt: In the lab, set pay-day saving to {labSave}. How much is set aside in a year? Type a number.
q7.hint: Read the green number in the lab.
q8.prompt: Keep {labSave} on pay day, and set the left-over to {labLeftQ}. How much more does paying first save in a year?
q8.hint: Read the Difference box in the lab.
q8.explain: {labYear} minus {labLeftYear} is {labGap}. Paying first saves far more.
t5.title: Challenge
t5.tradeoff: Paying first means less to spend each month. That is the point. Plan your spending around what remains, not the other way round.
t5.mistake: Many people think "I will save what is left". Money rarely stays left, because spending grows to match the money you have.
q9.prompt: Challenge: Meena's pay rises to {pay2}. On pay day she moves {rate2} of it to savings. How much does she set aside in a year?
q9.hint: First find the monthly amount: {rate2} of {pay2}. Then multiply by 12.
q9.explain: {rate2} of {pay2} is {mo2} a month. Over 12 months that is {yr2}.
glossary.save_savings.def: Money you set aside now instead of spending it.
glossary.save_pay_first.def: Setting savings aside on pay day, before any other spending.
glossary.save_habit.def: Saving a regular amount every month, whatever the size.
